parsed.explanation: The combined regime criminalises same-sex conduct (life imprisonment mainland) with documented police-lever use against LGBT people: 2018 witch hunt with forced anal examinations and torture, a police/lawyer/doctor committee to identify homosexuals, and torture of a nightclub arrestee in custody. A January 2024 report documents escalating sentiment and weaponisation of law; a June 2024 abduction and mutilation of a trans activist shows severe street violence with no documented prosecution. Government blocks LGBT websites; UN defenders cannot speak freely. Paper healthcare non-discrimination language (2010–2017) shows no enforcement. Both national and semi-autonomous statutes criminalise. No trans-specific criminal statute or execution is documented, but state-tolerated targeting plus custody torture places this in the High Risk band.

entry_documents.exposure: No trans-specific border or document rule is documented; the criminalisation framework creates latent exposure if a mismatch or device search reveals identity, but no visitor-facing entry practice is recorded.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy or phone search could feed into the documented police-lever pattern (arrest after nightclub outing).

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: torture in police custody of an LGBT detainee (2013 report — rape, beatings with canes/wires/pipes), 2018 forced anal examinations and torture during the declared witch hunt, arrest of a gay man leaving a nightclub.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No effective remedy for custody abuse appears in the record.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor pulled into any police encounter inherits this documented custody practice; sodomy provisions supply the charge.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Both regimes criminalise: mainland life imprisonment for sex between men; semi-autonomous jurisdiction's Penal Code (1934/2004) outlaws sex between women (up to five years) and its 2004 Penal Decree covers 'gross indecency' (three years). In-force status flagged unresolved.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Whichever jurisdiction the visitor enters, a criminal statute reaches them; the split adds no safe subnational option.

care_services.exposure: October 2017 deportation of HIV/AIDS group staff for 'promoting homosexuality', disrupting services; documented discrimination limiting rights enjoyment (Jan 2024 report).
care_services.protection: 2010 Nursing Regulations, 2013 Family Planning Guidelines, 2017 Respectful Care Guidelines bar discrimination by sexual orientation — paper commitments.
care_services.interaction: Paper protections coexist with documented service disruption; enforcement against discrimination is explicitly not established.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State-adjacent threat-framing: 2018 regional commissioner's 17-strong committee of police, lawyers, doctors to identify and punish homosexuals, scouring internet video; government-directed blocking of LGBTIQ websites (2024); weaponisation of law documented Jan 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2018 broadcast rules and 2020 media Code of Ethics bar hate speech on sexual orientation (enforcement unresolved); foreign ministry distanced itself from 2018 crackdown.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses both state and private action against visibly LGBT people; a visitor's online activity is itself monitored surface.

minors_guardians.exposure: Subnational 2004 Penal Decree sets sexual-offence age thresholds (absolute under 12, under-18 distinctions); a minor outed alongside a parent enters the same criminalisation and hostility climate.
minors_guardians.protection: Family planning language is age-inclusive; no youth-specific trans provision stated.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor adds dependency: the guardian's exposure becomes the child's, with no documented safeguard.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: June 2024: trans activist abducted by 12 men, found beaten in a forest with ears cut. Jan 2024 report documents escalating anti-LGBTI sentiment; Sept 2020 activists document prejudice, discrimination and violence. Pattern, not isolated anecdote.
street_violence_police_response.protection: UN condemnation of the 2024 attack flagging constitutional equality guarantees; named activists advocate openly.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: No prosecution of the 2018 perpetrators or 2017 deporters is documented — impunity corroborates recurrence; a visitor has no local network.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Freedom of speech and assembly declining; UN human rights defenders cannot make public statements supporting tolerance for fear of reprisals; Jan 2024 report documents weaponisation of law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional Article 13 equality guarantee exists; UN Human Rights Office issues condemnations.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Condemnations without documented investigation or prosecution show oversight recurring without remedying — corroboration of unremedied exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Oskara has morality sweeps, coerced statements, magistrates ignoring abuse and a doubtfully-applied capital clause. This dossier matches on torture/anal examinations by state actors and failing remedies, but lacks documented routine arrest of visitors for mere presentation or any credible capital pathway for identity — so slightly above.

Meridia has police shakedowns, overnight cells, oversight dismissing complaints, short jail terms. This dossier is harsher: documented custody torture, anal examinations, a state-adjacent identification committee, and life-imprisonment statutory exposure put it below this anchor.

Karthovia has unwritten identity checks and short detention with courts deferring to police but no imprisonment. This dossier documents criminal statutes with real enforcement levers, custody torture and a 2024 abduction — materially more severe, so well below 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is criminalisation plus state-tolerated targeting: sodomy/gross-indecency statutes with documented police use against LGBT people, forced anal examinations and torture in custody under an official identification committee, government blocking of LGBTIQ online spaces, and a 2024 abduction-mutilation of a trans activist with no documented prosecution. Paper healthcare non-discrimination commitments and media hate-speech codes show no enforcement and cannot offset the custody and street exposures. The semi-autonomous jurisdiction adds its own statutes, offering no safer region. No trans-specific criminal offence or execution is documented, and the most recent incident is mid-2024, but escalating sentiment, impaired civic space and absent remedies keep the rating at the boundary of High and Severe Risk. Travelling with a minor adds unmitigated dependency on the guardian's exposure.
